limitations: FreeREG's surname matching is exact and non-soundex, so its arm depends entirely on the twenty spellings actually queried.
The national parent pool does not reach every county set, which is why the county-set sweep is paired with it.
The county sweep covers eight counties only - Norfolk, Essex, Northamptonshire, Oxfordshire, Cambridgeshire, Middlesex, Westminster and Berkshire - so this is not an England-wide county-set negative.
The national parent search's variant engine is loose, so its eight Margaret rows are fuzzy-match noise rather than Gurney households; the negative rests on reading them, not on the count.

statement: Admitting Margaret to the mother axis changed no candidate score, because the axis was then searched and it is empty. Across FreeREG's 585 captured rows, five households carry a Margaret-family mother - Norwich 1638, Bardwell in Suffolk 1643 and 1645, and Mamble and Bayton in Worcestershire 1637 - and none has a father in the John family. Across 705 rows from eight FindMyPast county baptism sets, seven rows carry a Margaret-family mother, to fathers Robert, Edward, Michael and William, and none has a father in the John family at any date. The national cross-collection parent search bounded 1610-1650 returns eight rows for a father John with a mother Margaret, not one of them a genuine Gurney - the surname column reading '?', 'Fosse', 'G...Ds' and 'G?', fuzzy-match noise from Cornwall, Cheshire and Scotland. The negative is interpretable because the identical query shape with mother Mary returns the known Eythorne household and the Westminster Gurley household: the instrument was working when it returned nothing for Margaret.
